v.why: Replacing a removed edge 3 with a conv restores a direct input-to-output path, giving gains of +16 to +22 points, versus about zero when replacing another op.
Adding a 3x3 conv where edge 3 was absent gives a large gain, much more than swapping an existing op.
Reconnecting node 2 to the output through any op gives huge gains (+55 to +74) when edge 5 was none, while replacing an existing op gives a loss.
Filling an empty output edge with a 3x3 conv helps more than upgrading an existing op.
Upgrading a skip on edge 1 to a 3x3 conv gave +6 to +13 points on CIFAR in the observed cases.
Removing a skip on edge 3 can cut the only cheap input-to-output path, causing a very large drop.
Replacing a parameter-free pool with a learnable 3x3 conv on edge 4 gave +29 points in the observed case.
Swapping avg_pool on edge 4 for a conv gives consistent gains on all three datasets.
Replacing the pool with a skip on edge 4 improved all three datasets in the observed cases, unlike replacing a conv.
Downgrading a 3x3 conv on edge 5 to a pool hurts accuracy by 5 to 11 points.
